# Add the cell identities
Add the cell identities assigned by demuxlet to the metadata of the seurat object Na_va_data.
```{r}
# Add all the columns of the data dataframe to the metadata of the Seurat object
#Match the rows of demuxlet assignment "data" with the seurat metadata colum "BARCODE". because both have common barcodes
metadata_to_add_sc2glu.1 <- sc2glu.1[match(colnames(Na_va_data_sc2glu.1), sc2glu.1$BARCODE), ]
#Add the matching demuxlet identities to the metadata
Na_va_data_sc2glu.1 <- AddMetaData(Na_va_data_sc2glu.1, metadata = metadata_to_add_sc2glu.1)


metadata_to_add_sc2glu.2 <- sc2glu.2[match(colnames(Na_va_data_sc2glu.2), sc2glu.2$BARCODE), ]
#Add the matching demuxlet identities to the metadata
Na_va_data_sc2glu.2 <- AddMetaData(Na_va_data_sc2glu.2, metadata = metadata_to_add_sc2glu.2)
```
We do this because DGY3 was part of a separate pool and it formed a different cluster from all the other strains. We removed KANMX and NATMX because these barcoded antibiotic markers were added in the DGY3 to identify them.

```{r}
SeuratObj <- merge(Na_va_data_sc2glu.1_after, y = Na_va_data_sc2glu.2_after, 
                       add.cell.ids = c("Sample1", "Sample2"))


#Perform these before integration 
SeuratObj <- NormalizeData(SeuratObj)
SeuratObj <- FindVariableFeatures(SeuratObj)
SeuratObj <- ScaleData(SeuratObj)
SeuratObj <- RunPCA(SeuratObj)
SeuratObj <- FindNeighbors(SeuratObj, dims = 1:30, reduction = "pca")
SeuratObj <- FindClusters(SeuratObj, resolution = 1.5, cluster.name = "unintegrated_clusters")

#before integration
DimPlot(SeuratObj, reduction = "umap.unintegrated", group.by = "SNG.BEST.GUESS", label = TRUE)

#DimPlot(SeuratObj, reduction = "umap.unintegrated", group.by = "Quality_Category")

#integration
SeuratObj_Integrated <- IntegrateLayers(
  object = SeuratObj, method = CCAIntegration,
  orig.reduction = "pca", new.reduction = "integrated.cca",
  verbose = FALSE
)

SeuratObj_Integrated <- FindNeighbors(SeuratObj_Integrated, reduction = "integrated.cca", dims = 1:30)
SeuratObj_Integrated <- FindClusters(SeuratObj_Integrated, resolution = 2, cluster.name = "cca_clusters")

SeuratObj_Integrated <- RunUMAP(SeuratObj_Integrated, reduction = "integrated.cca", dims = 1:30, reduction.name = "umap.cca")

DimPlot(SeuratObj_Integrated, reduction = "umap.cca", group.by = "SNG.BEST.GUESS", label = TRUE)
DimPlot(SeuratObj_Integrated, reduction = "umap.cca", group.by = "orig.ident")
DimPlot(SeuratObj_Integrated, reduction = "umap.cca", group.by = "cca_clusters", label = TRUE)
```

```{r}
counts_layer2 <- SeuratObj[["RNA"]]$counts.2[common_genes, ]

# Now combine

# Verify
dim(counts_matrix)
```

###Actual pseudobulking
## 1. Get the count_matrix and metadata. 
```{r}
#create a metadata dataframe
metadata_df <- SeuratObj_Integrated@meta.data
```
#save the seurat_obj
```{r}
# Save the merged/integrated single-cell object (raw counts + SNG.BEST.GUESS)

saveRDS(SeuratObj_Integrated,
        file = "Na_va_data_subsetted_sc2glu_replicates_merged.rds")
cat("Saved merged Seurat object:", ncol(SeuratObj_Integrated), "cells,",
    nrow(SeuratObj_Integrated), "genes\n")
```

## 2. Extract genotype information from metadata
```{r}
# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(42)

genotypes <- unique(metadata_df$SNG.BEST.GUESS)
cat("Found", length(genotypes), "unique genotypes:", paste(genotypes, collapse=", "), "\n")

# Create a list to store cell counts per genotype
cell_counts_per_genotype <- list()

#save this genotype list in a .txt file, where each strain is one line only. So this file must have 71 lines
write.table(genotypes, 
            file = "../fastlmm/codes/genotype_file/strain_list_71.txt",
            row.names = FALSE,
            col.names = FALSE,
            quote = FALSE)


```
## 3. Create lists to store pseudobulk results
```{r}
pseudobulk_sum_counts <- list()  # For sum aggregation
```
## 4. Perform pseudobulk aggregation for each genotype using both methods
This for loop will go over metadata data and extract rownames which are cells based on genotype, it will check if there are cells per genotype. subset the count matrix using cell barcode per genotype and then do rowsums and rowmeans then store the count
```{r}

# Pseudobulk script with minimal changes
for (genotype in genotypes) {
  # Get cell barcodes for this genotype from integrated object's metadata
  cells_in_genotype <- rownames(metadata_df[metadata_df$SNG.BEST.GUESS == genotype, ])
  
  # Skip if no cells found for this genotype
  if (length(cells_in_genotype) == 0) {
    cat("No cells found for genotype:", genotype, "\n")
    next
  }
  
  cat("Processing genotype:", genotype, "with", length(cells_in_genotype), "cells\n")
  
  # Subset the counts matrix to include only cells of this genotype
  # Use the pre-computed counts_matrix with common genes
  genotype_counts <- counts_matrix[, cells_in_genotype, drop = FALSE]
  
  # Sum aggregation (standard pseudobulk approach)
  pseudobulk_sum_counts[[genotype]] <- rowSums(genotype_counts)
  
  # Store the cell count for this genotype
  cell_counts_per_genotype[[genotype]] <- length(cells_in_genotype)
}
```
## 5. Convert the lists to data frames
The first two dataframes includes sum count for each gene in each genotype 
and the third dataframe "cell_counts_df" includes total number of cells per genotype
```{r}
pseudobulk_sum_df <- as.data.frame(do.call(cbind, pseudobulk_sum_counts))
colnames(pseudobulk_sum_df) <- names(pseudobulk_sum_counts)

pseudobulk_sum_df

write.csv(pseudobulk_sum_df, file = "../fastlmm/data/pheno_data/pseudobulked_sc2glu_before_any_filtering.csv")
```
#Selection of expressed transcripts (atleast 5 counts across 8 strains)
```{r}
#keep only the commonly expressed transcripts
# Step 1: Calculate the 50% threshold - genes are expressed in 40% of the strain
n_samples <- ncol(pseudobulk_sum_df)  # Total number of strains
threshold <- n_samples * 0.6          # 50% threshold

# Step 2: Count how many samples each gene is expressed in (> 0)
present_counts <- rowSums(pseudobulk_sum_df > 0)

# Step 3: Filter to keep only genes expressed in >= 40% of samples
reliable_transcripts <- pseudobulk_sum_df[present_counts >= threshold, ]

pseudobulk_sum_df <- reliable_transcripts



library(DESeq2)
# Sum aggregation - direct normalization with DESeq2
# Create metadata for sum data
condition_sum <- factor(colnames(pseudobulk_sum_df))
coldata_sum <- data.frame(row.names = colnames(pseudobulk_sum_df), condition = condition_sum)

# Create DESeq dataset and normalize
dds_sum <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = round(as.matrix(pseudobulk_sum_df)), # DESeq2 expects integers
  colData = coldata_sum,
  design = ~ 1
)
dds_sum <- estimateSizeFactors(dds_sum)
sum_normalized_df <- counts(dds_sum, normalized = TRUE)

write.csv(sum_normalized_df, file = "../fastlmm/data/pheno_data/pseudobulked_data_sc2glu.csv")
```

#After gene location file, convert common name to ORF
```{r}
# Build a simple common name -> ORF lookup from the annotation file
common_to_orf <- all_custom_gene_annotations %>%
  filter(!is.na(gene_name), !is.na(gene_id)) %>%
  distinct(gene_name, gene_id) %>%
  deframe()  # creates named vector: names = gene_name, values = gene_id

# Get gene IDs from rownames of gene_matrix
expr_gene_ids <- rownames(gene_matrix)

# Identify which are already ORFs
is_orf <- grepl("^Y[A-Z]{2}\\d{3}[WC](-[A-Z])?$", expr_gene_ids)
cat("Already ORF format:", sum(is_orf), "\n")
cat("Common names to convert:", sum(!is_orf), "\n")

# Map common names to ORF using annotation file
expr_orf_ids <- ifelse(
  is_orf,
  expr_gene_ids,
  ifelse(expr_gene_ids %in% names(common_to_orf), common_to_orf[expr_gene_ids], expr_gene_ids)
)

# Report
cat("Converted:", sum(!is_orf & expr_gene_ids %in% names(common_to_orf)), "\n")
cat("Could not convert:", sum(!is_orf & !expr_gene_ids %in% names(common_to_orf)), "\n")

# Show names that could not be converted
not_converted <- expr_gene_ids[!is_orf & !expr_gene_ids %in% names(common_to_orf)]
cat("Genes that could not be converted:\n")
print(not_converted)


# Replace rownames BEFORE removing any rows
rownames(gene_matrix) <- expr_orf_ids
```

Add rownames as first column, remove rownames. There are 5093 rows because 5093 genes are expressed. I want to make and 5093 files where each file is saved as gene_name.txt and format for each file is

strain    gene
strain A   12
strain B   23

i.e., the strain column is repeated in each phenotype 
```{r}
# R Script to split gene expression data into individual gene files
# Each file will have strain information repeated for each gene

# Load required library
library(data.table)

# Read the phenotype file (adjust the file path as needed)
# Assuming the file has strain names as rownames and genes as columns
pheno_file <- "../fastlmm/data/pheno_data/pheno_data_fastlmm_sc2glu.txt"  # Replace with your actual file path
output_dir <- "../fastlmm/data/splitted_pheno_file_per_gene"  # Output directory for individual gene files

# Read the data
# Assuming tab-separated file with rownames as strain names
df <- read.csv(pheno_file, sep="\t", row.names=1, header=TRUE)

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Get strain names (from rownames)
strain_names <- rownames(df)

# Get gene names (from column names)
gene_names <- colnames(df)

print(paste("Processing", length(gene_names), "genes for", length(strain_names), "strains"))

# Process each gene
for (i in 1:length(gene_names)) {
  gene_name <- gene_names[i]
  
  # Create a data frame for this gene (without gene column)
  gene_data <- data.frame(
    strain = strain_names,
    value = df[, i],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  # Set column names - strain and gene name
  colnames(gene_data) <- c("strain", gene_name)
  
  # Create output filename
  output_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(gene_name, ".txt"))
  
  # Write the file (tab-separated, no row names, with header)
  write.table(gene_data, 
              file = output_file, 
              sep = "\t", 
              row.names = FALSE, 
              col.names = TRUE, 
              quote = FALSE)
  
  # Progress indicator
  if (i %% 500 == 0) {
    print(paste("Processed", i, "genes..."))
  }
}

print(paste("Completed! Created", length(gene_names), "gene files in", output_dir, "directory"))

# Example: Show the first few lines of the first gene file
if (length(gene_names) > 0) {
  first_gene_file <- file.path(output_dir, paste0(gene_names[1], ".txt"))
  if (file.exists(first_gene_file)) {
    print(paste("Example content of", paste0(gene_names[1], ".txt"), ":"))
    example_content <- read.table(first_gene_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", nrows = 5)
    print(example_content)
  }
}
```

# This chunk will perform rank based Inverse normal transformation
#!/usr/bin/env Rscript
## ---------------------------
##
## Script name: rank_based_Inverse_Normal_Transformation.r
##
## Purpose of script: Perform the rank-based INT from a phenotype file
##
## Author: Akriti
##
## Date Created: 2025-10-11
##
## ---------------------------
##
## Notes: Takes a phenotypes in .tsv format (but .txt extension), 
##        that is a tsv file with for each row:
##        Strain      Condition
##        XXX         1563
##        XXX         4563
##        ....
##
##        The pheno file can contain NAs, which will be kept in the output file. 
##        The output file is a tsv file containing 2 columns:
##        Strain  Normalized value
##
## ---------------------------


Verify on a single file
```{r}
library(stringr)
## ---------------------------
rank.based.INT <- function(x, c=3/8, method="average")
{
  # This function performs the rank-based inverse normal transformation (INT)
  # If method is "average" ties will share the same average value. 
  # If method is "random", ties are given rank randomly
  # Formula found in Beasley 2009 with an offset of c=3/8 as recommended in Blom 1958
  
  r <- rank(x, ties.method = method)
  r[is.na(x)] <- NA # reput NA values in the vector because rank() gives a rank to NAs
  N <- length(x[!is.na(x)])
  qnorm((r-c)/(N-2*c+1))
}

# HARDCODED INPUT FILE PATH - Change this to your input file
phenotypesPath <- "../fastlmm/data/splitted_pheno_file_per_gene/YDL248W.txt"

# HARDCODED OUTPUT DIRECTORY - Change this to your desired output path
output_directory <- "../fastlmm/data/normalized_pheno_file"
# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
dir.create(output_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Read the input file to get original column names
input_df <- read.csv(file = phenotypesPath, header = T, sep = "\t")
original_colnames <- colnames(input_df)

# Get file name (for output file naming)
fileName <- basename(phenotypesPath)
fileName <- str_remove(fileName, ".txt")

# Convert the phenotypes to a single vector
phenotypes <- input_df[,2]
# Get the strains list in a vector
strainList <- input_df[,1]

# Normalization with the rank-based INT function
normalized.phenotypes <- rank.based.INT(x = phenotypes)

# Converting to dataframe with original column names
normalized.phenotypes.df <- data.frame(strainList, normalized.phenotypes)
colnames(normalized.phenotypes.df) <- original_colnames

# removing NA values for the final file
normalized.phenotypes.df.noNA <- na.omit(normalized.phenotypes.df)

# Exporting to tsv file in the hardcoded output directory
newPath <- file.path(output_directory, paste0(fileName, ".norm.txt"))
print(paste("Output file:", newPath))
write.table(normalized.phenotypes.df.noNA, file = newPath, row.names = F, col.names = T, sep = "\t", quote = F)
```
Run it on all the files in the folder
```{r}
library(stringr)
## ---------------------------
rank.based.INT <- function(x, c=3/8, method="average")
{
  # This function performs the rank-based inverse normal transformation (INT)
  # If method is "average" ties will share the same average value. 
  # If method is "random", ties are given rank randomly
  # Formula found in Beasley 2009 with an offset of c=3/8 as recommended in Blom 1958
  
  r <- rank(x, ties.method = method)
  r[is.na(x)] <- NA # reput NA values in the vector because rank() gives a rank to NAs
  N <- length(x[!is.na(x)])
  qnorm((r-c)/(N-2*c+1))
}

# HARDCODED INPUT DIRECTORY - Change this to your input directory
input_directory <- "../fastlmm/data/splitted_pheno_file_per_gene/"

# HARDCODED OUTPUT DIRECTORY - Change this to your desired output path
output_directory <- "../fastlmm/data/normalized_pheno_file"

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
dir.create(output_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Get list of all .txt files in input directory
phenotype_files <- list.files(path = input_directory, pattern = "\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE)

print(paste("Found", length(phenotype_files), "phenotype files to process"))

# Process each file
for (phenotypesPath in phenotype_files) {
  
  print(paste("Processing:", basename(phenotypesPath)))
  
  # Read the input file to get original column names
  input_df <- read.csv(file = phenotypesPath, header = T, sep = "\t")
  original_colnames <- colnames(input_df)
  
  # Get file name (for output file naming)
  fileName <- basename(phenotypesPath)
  fileName <- str_remove(fileName, ".txt")
  
  # Convert the phenotypes to a single vector
  phenotypes <- input_df[,2]
  # Get the strains list in a vector
  strainList <- input_df[,1]
  
  # Normalization with the rank-based INT function
  normalized.phenotypes <- rank.based.INT(x = phenotypes)
  
  # Converting to dataframe with original column names
  normalized.phenotypes.df <- data.frame(strainList, normalized.phenotypes)
  colnames(normalized.phenotypes.df) <- original_colnames
  
  # removing NA values for the final file
  normalized.phenotypes.df.noNA <- na.omit(normalized.phenotypes.df)
  
  # Exporting to tsv file in the hardcoded output directory
  newPath <- file.path(output_directory, paste0(fileName, ".norm.txt"))
  write.table(normalized.phenotypes.df.noNA, file = newPath, row.names = F, col.names = T, sep = "\t", quote = F)
}

print(paste("Completed! Processed", length(phenotype_files), "files"))
print(paste("Output directory:", output_directory))
```
